headline: Apple's inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb
summary: The tech giant's inventory jumped to $14.54 billion in Q4, with CEO John Ternus calling current memory pricing "unprecedented."
details: Apple's inventory saw a significant increase in its fiscal fourth-quarter, climbing 31.1% from $11.09 billion in Q3 to $14.54 billion in Q4. This represents a year-over-year surge of 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the same quarter last year.
The company's gross margin forecast of 45% to 46% for the December quarter is largely influenced by the rising costs of memory chips. Apple reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.

CEO John Ternus described the current memory pricing as "unprecedented," noting that higher costs in the September quarter were partially offset by inventory benefits and lower costs for other components. He anticipates even higher memory costs in the December quarter.

To mitigate these costs, Apple implemented price increases on some devices, including Macs and iPads in June and iPhones in September. However, the company expects memory costs to continue increasing beyond December.

Apple's supply chain operations are also being impacted, with manufacturing purchase obligations increasing by $33 billion from June to September. This increase is expected to be reflected in their upcoming annual filing.

Supply constraints due to these issues also affected iPad sales, which were one of the few product segments that did not grow. iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, falling short of analysts' expectations and down 10% from the previous year.

headline: Anthropic close to AI self-improvement capability, warns filing
summary: AI lab Anthropic has disclosed in a filing that it may soon meet its own definition of 'recursive self-improvement' (RSI), a point where AI accelerates its own development.
details: Anthropic has disclosed in a regulatory filing that it may be on the verge of achieving Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a state where AI models become capable of significantly accelerating their own development.

RSI is a critical milestone in AI advancement. For AI doomers, it represents a potential loss of human control, leading to unpredictable outcomes. Conversely, enthusiasts see it as a gateway to unprecedented productivity and scientific discovery.

The filing states that Anthropic has previously used AI to develop new models whose capabilities advanced rapidly without immediate recognition. It warns that this acceleration poses a considerable safety risk, especially if it outpaces the development of corresponding safety and alignment measures.

While Anthropic has not yet designated any current models as exceeding the RSI threshold, internal assessments suggest they may imminently meet the criteria for 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.'

The company has also stated that it does not anticipate being able to fully autonomously design and build future frontier models without meaningful human supervision. Updates to its Responsible Scaling Policy are being considered to ensure human control over frontier model development.

Skeptics may view these claims as a form of marketing within the S-1 filing, aiming to highlight the company's advanced capabilities. However, the rapid improvements in Claude's coding, math, and cybersecurity skills lend credence to Anthropic's concerns.
